findings.interpretation: The panel is sick (only 4% low complexity), but the 99215 share is 2 to 8 times the peer rate at every complexity level, and the random charts often support a lower level than billed. Overpayment estimate from the random sample is reliable: point $2,154 (CI $1,153 to $3,154). One unsigned note was excluded.

findings.headline: 17 of 45 charts (random plus targeted 99215) support a lower level than billed; 35% of documented 99214/99215 in the random sample were below the billed level (peer 4%)
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 9.2 times expected on a mostly low-complexity panel (65%). The charts disagree with the billed level. The random-sample dollar estimate is NOT reliable (only 3 charts in the 99215 stratum), so do not quote a figure.

findings.headline: 73% of 22 documented 99215 claims are below the billed level (peer 0%); 19 of 45 charts are below billed
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 5.4 times expected. A random sample was followed by a targeted 99215 sample, and both point the same way. The dollar estimate is not reliable (7 charts in the 99215 stratum, 8 needed).

findings.headline: Healthy panel (80% low complexity) billed 99215 at 11 times expected; the notes support the billed level but look inflated
findings.interpretation: No chart was below the billed level, but 40% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, 17% describe data review that the claim's lab lines cannot back, and the audit trail shows bulk-created (7%) and paste-heavy (10%) notes. 99215 runs 15 to 24% even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions. This is weaker than chart-rule evidence: it rests on rates of note signals, and honest practices show some of these too. A human coder should review it first.

findings.headline: Highest screen score (z_adj 10.2, 12.7 times expected); notes look inflated: 50% address fewer problems than claimed, 35% signed late, 50% duplicated
findings.interpretation: The 99215 share is 22 to 29% for patients with 0 or 1 conditions (peers 2 to 3%). The random request first came back with wrong dates, and only 6 random charts were usable. A targeted 99215 request filled out the set, so the sample is mixed and supports no overpayment estimate. Only 1 of 26 charts was below the billed level; the leaning rests on note-inflation signals and needs human review.

findings.headline: 6 of 45 charts below billed level; result sits between the rule's cutoffs
findings.interpretation: In the random sample, 3 of 6 99215 charts were below the billed level, but the larger set (random plus targeted) gives 13%, which is borderline. 44% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies. The panel is healthy (88% low complexity), so this is worth a human look but does not meet the bar.

findings.headline: 99215 share 6.7 times expected and elevated at every complexity level, but 29 of 30 charts support the billed level
findings.interpretation: The audit trail shows paste-heavy (23%) and bulk-created (17%) notes, with 20% duplication and 13% late signing. Those are elevated, but the review did not flag the notes as inflated. The concern is unresolved; human coder review of the audit-trail examples (e.g. C0084256, C0084267, C0084409) is suggested.

findings.headline: Documentation supports billing (2 of 29 below billed); audit trail clean
